docs.title: Claude for Trading
docs.text: Dark trading-terminal Streamlit dashboard with three analytical pages: regime detection, sensitivity analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page Description Regime Detection HMM-based market regime classification with online forward filtering Sensitivity Analysis Parameter robustness scoring via single-parameter sweeps Monte Carlo Equity curve probability cloud from trade-return shuffling

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
claude-for-trading/
├── home.py                  # Landing page
├── design_system.py         # Shared theme, colors, Plotly layouts, HTML helpers
├── demo/demo.py             # Design system walkthrough
├── pages/
│   ├── dashboard.py         # HMM regime detection
│   ├── sensitivity_analysis.py  # Parameter sensitivity sweep
│   └── monte_carlo.py       # Monte Carlo equity simulation
└── requirements.txt         # Python dependencies

docs.title: Design System
docs.text:
design_system.py provides shared building blocks:

  • Theme — apply_theme() injects dark CSS
  • HTML helpers — metric_card(), regime_badge(), section_header(), status_dot(), pnl_color()
  • Plotly — get_plotly_layout() returns dark-themed Plotly dict
  • Data — style_dataframe() applies dark formatting to pandas DataFrames
  • Colors — constants: BG_PRIMARY, ACCENT_CYAN, ACCENT_GREEN, ACCENT_RED, ACCENT_AMBER, REGIME_COLORS

See Design System for the full reference.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
streamlit run home.py

docs.title: URL Routing
docs.text:
Dashboard and Sensitivity pages support path-based routing via URL query params:

  • ?ticker=SPY&start_date=2021-01-01&end_date=2024-01-01 — auto-runs with those params
  • URL updates as you change inputs — shareable links

docs.title: Design System
docs.text:
Shared design system used by all dashboard pages. Import via:

from design_system import *

apply_theme()

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
apply_theme() injects dark trading-terminal CSS:

  • Fonts: DM Sans (UI text), JetBrains Mono (code/numbers)
  • Background: #0a0a0f primary, #12121a cards
  • Accent: #00d4ff cyan (primary accent)
  • Top bar: 2px cyan line via ::before pseudo-element
  • Chrome removed: main menu, sidebar nav, footer hidden

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
BG_PRIMARY = "#0a0a0f"          # Main background
BG_CARD = "#12121a"             # Card background

docs.title: metric_card(label, value, color)
docs.text:
Renders a metric display with uppercase label and large value:

st.markdown(metric_card("PnL", "+$12,345", ACCENT_GREEN), unsafe_allow_html=True)

docs.title: regime_badge(regime_name, confidence=None)
docs.text:
Renders a colored pill/badge with optional confidence percentage:

st.markdown(regime_badge("Low Vol", confidence=87.3), unsafe_allow_html=True)

docs.title: section_header(text)
docs.text:
Renders an uppercase section header with divider line:

st.markdown(section_header("Performance"), unsafe_allow_html=True)

docs.title: status_dot(status)
docs.text:
Renders a colored dot indicator (green for connected/active, red for disconnected/error, amber for warning):

st.markdown(status_dot("connected") + " Connected", unsafe_allow_html=True)

docs.title: pnl_color(value)
docs.text:
Returns ACCENT_GREEN if value ≥ 0, ACCENT_RED if value < 0:

color = pnl_color(-500)  # Returns ACCENT_RED

docs.title: get_plotly_layout(**overrides)
docs.text:
Returns a base Plotly layout dict with dark trading-terminal styling. Pass keyword overrides to merge:

layout = get_plotly_layout(
    xaxis=dict(title="Date", type="date"),
    yaxis=dict(title="Price ($)", tickformat="$,.0f"),
    height=450,
)
fig = go.Figure(layout=layout)

docs.title: style_dataframe(df)
docs.text:
Returns a pandas Styler with dark formatting:

styled = style_dataframe(df)
styled = styled.format({
    "PnL": lambda v: f"${v:,.0f}",
    "Return": "{:.1%}",
})
st.dataframe(styled, width="stretch", hide_index=True)

docs.title: Monte Carlo Simulation
docs.text: Equity curve probability cloud from trade-return shuffling.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Shuffles historical trade returns, adds noise, and runs many simulations to estimate probability distributions of outcomes. Tests for overfitting by comparing original backtest result against shuffled permutations.

docs.title: Data Input
docs.text:
• Upload CSV with columns: date, trade_return
  • Or use built-in sample data — 200 trades with slight positive edge (+0.15% per trade) and loss clustering

docs.title: Simulation Engine
docs.text:
for each simulation i:
    shuffled = permute(trade_returns) + noise(±0.3%)
    equity[t+1] = equity[t] * (1 + shuffled[t])

Default: 1,000 simulations, starting capital $100,000.

docs.title: Probability Metrics
docs.text:
• Probability of loss — % of simulations where final value < starting capital
  • Probability of 20%+ drawdown — % of simulations with max drawdown ≥ 20%
  • Probability of 30%+ drawdown — % of simulations with max drawdown ≥ 30%

docs.title: Percentile Distribution
docs.text: • 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentiles of max drawdown distribution

docs.title: Overfitting Check
docs.text:
Compares original backtest final value against shuffled outcomes:

original_pctile = mean(final_values < original_final_value)
  • >90th percentile — HIGH risk: original result looks too good, possible overfitting
  • >80th percentile — MEDIUM risk
  • ≤80th percentile — LOW risk

docs.title: Fan Chart
docs.text:
Cinematic probability cloud showing:

  • Individual curves — low opacity lines (0.015) in cyan
  • 5th–95th band — wide probability range
  • 25th–75th band — interquartile range
  • Median line — 50th percentile
  • Original backtest — solid white line

docs.title: Histograms
docs.text:
• Final portfolio values — distribution of ending values with original backtest line
  • Max drawdown distribution — distribution of worst drawdowns per simulation

docs.title: Drawdown Distribution Detail
docs.text: 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentile values displayed as cards.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text: Auto-generated text summarizing probability of loss, drawdowns, median outcome, and original backtest percentile.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Upload CSV or use sample data
  2. Set starting capital and number of simulations
  3. Click "Run Simulation"

docs.title: Regime Detection
docs.text: HMM-based market regime classification with online forward filtering. No look-ahead bias.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The regime detection page downloads price data, engineers features, trains a Hidden Markov Model, and produces regime-colored price charts with confidence timelines.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
1. Data download via yfinance
  2. Feature engineering: log returns, 20-day realized vol, volume ratio, H-L range
  3. Model selection: trains hmmlearn.GaussianHMM (diagonal covariance) with 3–7 regimes, selects via BIC
  4. Forward-filtered labels: uses forward algorithm (alpha) to compute posterior marginals gamma[t] = P(q_t | o_1..t) — NO model.predict() used
  5. Stability filter: regimes must persist 3 consecutive bars; >4 transitions in 20-bar window flags as "Uncertain"
  6. Regime labeling: sorts by mean volatility — Low Vol / Medium Vol / High Vol

docs.title: No Look-Ahead Guarantee
docs.text:
The page verifies no look-ahead bias on every run:

def verify_no_lookahead() -> bool:
    """Confirm no look-ahead bias — Viterbi decoding must not be used."""
    # Scans source code for model.predict() or model.predict_proba() calls
    # Returns True if clean, False if found

If model.predict() is found in the code, the page displays an error and aborts.

docs.title: Forward Filtering
docs.text:
Instead of calling model.predict() (which uses Viterbi and requires all observations), the page computes forward-filtered labels using the forward algorithm:

alpha[t, j] = sum_i(alpha[t-1, i] * trans[i,j]) * b_j(o_t)
gamma[t, i] = alpha[t, i] / sum_j(alpha[t, j])   # posterior marginals
label[t] = argmax_i(gamma[t, i])
confidence[t] = max(gamma[t, i])

This means label at time T uses only data 1..T — zero look-ahead bias.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Enter ticker (default: SPY)
  2. Set date range (default: last 3 years)
  3. Optionally override #regimes (0 = auto-select via BIC)
  4. Click "Run Analysis"

docs.title: Visualizations
docs.text:
• Price chart with regime-colored background bands (opacity 0.13)
  • Regime statistics cards — mean return, vol, vol ratio, time in regime
  • Confidence timeline — area chart colored by regime, showing posterior probability

docs.text:
Supports shareable links:

docs.title: Sensitivity Analysis
docs.text: Parameter robustness scoring via single-parameter sweeps on a MA-crossover strategy.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Tests how stable a strategy's performance is when individual parameters change. Built-in demo uses a simple moving average crossover on SPY.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
• Buy: fast MA crosses above slow MA
  • Sell: fast MA crosses below slow MA, or stop-loss/take-profit hit

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Base Range Step fast_ma 10 5–30 1 slow_ma 50 20–100 5 stop_loss_pct 2.0 0.5–5.0 0.5 take_profit_pct 4.0 1.0–10.0 0.5

docs.title: Robustness Scoring
docs.text:
For each parameter, holds all others constant and sweeps the target across its range. Scores 0–100 based on coefficient of variation (CV) of performance:

cv = std(values) / abs(mean(values))
score = max(0, min(100, 100 * (1 - cv)))
  • CV=0 → score=100 (perfectly stable)
  • CV=1 → score=50
  • CV=2 → score=0

When base value has no trades (all returns are 0), scores all points equally — no degradation possible.

docs.title: Classification
docs.text:
• ≥70 Robust (green) — performance stays stable across range
  • 40–70 Moderate (amber) — some sensitivity, consider tightening range
  • <40 Fragile (red) — small changes cause large swings, possible overfitting

docs.title: Overall Robustness Gauge
docs.text: Circular arc meter showing the average of all parameter scores. Colored green/amber/red by classification.

docs.title: Degradation Heatmap
docs.text:
Parameters on Y-axis, metrics on X-axis. Cells colored by degradation from base performance:

  • Deep green (≤10% degradation)
  • Cyan (≤20%)
  • Amber (≤40%)
  • Red (>40%)

docs.title: Per-Parameter Detail Charts
docs.text: Line charts showing total return vs parameter value. Base value marked with dashed cyan line. Stable zone (within 20% of base) shown as a subtle green-tinted background band.

docs.text: Toggle "Use custom ranges" in the sidebar to override parameter ranges.
